references.text: The preceding context establishes the law concerning an ox that gores a person to death and the liability of its owner if the ox was known to be dangerous.
Equal treatment of men and women in certain legal contexts, reflecting the principle that the same penalty applies whether it is a son or daughter who is injured.
Another example of Mosaic law applying the same standard regardless of the victim's gender or age.
The principle of one law for all, where the same penalty must apply regardless of who is involved.
Exodus 21:31 is a direct application of the lex talionis principle from Leviticus 24:19 to harm inflicted upon children.
Both verses establish the principle that loss of life under the hand of a master or ruler requires vengeance, regardless of the victim's status (slave or child).
